text.p: Julius Meinl International, the east European arm of Austrian supermarket chain Julius Meinl AG, said on Wednesday it posted strong growth in earnings and sales last year.
In a statement, the firm said its preliminary operating profit was up 35 percent to 199 million schillings and turnover up 27 percent to five billion schillings.
Pre-tax profit growth outstripped the increase in operating profit and sales, it continued, without giving further details.
Meinl forecast it would add another 30-40 percent to sales this year, mainly in the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland.
In 1996, sales through its 194 stores in Hungary were up 37.6 percent to 3.2 billion schillings and pre-tax profit up 30.4 percent to 95 million.
Sales through its 65 outlets in the Czech Republic increased 41.2 percent to 1.5 billion schillings and pre-tax profit soared 118 percent to around 70 million schillings.
Its coffee business in Slovakia, Italy and Slovenia posted a pre-tax profit of 29 million schillings, a rise of 37.03 percent, despite lower turnover.
Meinl said it planned an American Depository Receipt listing in New York in the first half of this year. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
